Structures read their type_id straight out of a static 64-record array in the CodeOverlay (records 0xAC bytes, name inline, type_id is the byte 5 before the name, first record TMPL at ROM 0x165FDC). _meta._note: CNC3D N64 type-code -> mesh mapping. Meshes are OBJs in share/CNC3D/assets/models_table/, named dl_<ROMoffset>.
_meta.method: code-derived. The game keeps ONE unified object-type enum shared by structures, units, aircraft and civilian buildings, and model_index = type_id + 10. Structures read their type_id straight out of a static 64-record array in the CodeOverlay (records 0xAC bytes, name inline, type_id is the byte 5 before the name, first record TMPL at ROM 0x165FDC). Units and aircraft get theirs as the first stack argument (sp+0x10) to their type-class constructors: UnitTypeClass ctor 0x801E92F0 called 16x from ROM 0x18B8A8, AircraftTypeClass ctor 0x801F3C70 called 5x from ROM 0x196058. Verified by rendering every slot from four angles; see work/vmap_struct2.png, work/vmap_units2.png, work/angles.png, work/angles2.png.
negative_results: Spawn_Model at RAM 0x8004BB9C is NOT the unit path and is a dead end for this mapping. Whole-ROM scans: the model table 0x80099998 has exactly 2 code references (Spawn_Model's index at ROM 0x004C7CC and an init loop at 0x0057160); there are exactly 7 jal sites to Spawn_Model, all with constant indices 1,3,4,5,6,7,8,9; and there are ZERO literal function pointers to it, so it is never called indirectly. Spawn_Model only ever places menu/intro models.

The unit ctor argument at sp+0x14 looks like a model index (32-49, with 255 for MHQ/LST/BOAT/A10/C17) but is NOT one: it fails the pixel test, since it puts models at empty slots 34/35/49 and claims A10 has no model when slot 50 is plainly an A-10. It is a cameo/build-list index; 255 means 'not buildable'.

There is no type->modelIndex lookup ARRAY anywhere in the ROM. A whole-ROM scan for an ascending byte run 55..91 (any stride) and 134..140 returns nothing usable. The mapping is arithmetic (id+10), not a table.

CodeOverlay (ROM 0x01643F0-0x01B67D0) contains ZERO data pointers and zero lui/addiu-built addresses into GameModelsGeometry, so the string pools next to 0x1690D0 are not adjacent to any model pointer table.
GAME_STATE_LAYERS-style scene graph in the tail of GameModelsGeometry (class tags CAFEDEAD/DEADCAFE/BEEFED02/FEEB000n at 0x800AC2C0..0x800AC3A0) is a serialized object graph, but it carries no names.
The second table at 0x80099750 (29 entries) is the UI cursor set (arrows, wrench, Nod logo, dollar sign), not turrets.

The earlier tree mapping (T01=113..T18=130, SPLIT2=131) was off by one from T09 onward because it assumed the tree ids were contiguous. Id 111 is skipped, so T09 starts at slot 122 and SPLIT2 shares slot 132 with SPLIT3 rather than owning 131. The visual anchors (rock block, golden crown) could not detect that, since the mis-assigned slots hold look-alike trees.
_meta.segments_note: Nine of these models live in the ScriptModels segment (RAM 0x80122B60-0x801360E0, ROM = RAM - 0x8005BCC0), not GameModelsGeometry: TMPL, FACT, SAM, FTNK, STNK, HTNK, BOAT, TRAN, ORCA. They are exactly the models with moving parts. Earlier passes used 0x80130830 as the end of ScriptModels, which is wrong (that is ReplayMission's RAM base); with the correct bound these nine stop rendering blank.

table_blocks.0-9: menu / intro models. Confirmed independently: these are the ONLY indices Spawn_Model (RAM 0x8004BB9C) is ever called with (constants 1,3,4,5,6,7,8,9 at ROM 0x004ED74-0x004EE54). This is why the unified type enum is offset by +10.
table_blocks.108-112: NULL (game type ids 98-102). Unclaimed: no terrain, structure, unit or civilian type registers these. They are NOT the tree clumps.
table_blocks.113-132: terrain trees, RESOLVED by lookup. TerrainTypeClass registration chain at ROM 0x018CE30: T01..T08 = ids 103-110 (slots 113-120), T09..T18 = ids 112-121 (slots 122-131), SPLIT2 and SPLIT3 BOTH = id 122 (slot 132, the blossom tree). Id 111 / slot 121 is unclaimed. Only 8 distinct tree meshes exist and the ROM's own record array repeats their 8 Gfx pointers with period 8 from slot 113, so T01/T16, T02/T09/T17, T03/T10/T18 etc. share a mesh. That repetition is read out of the ROM, not synthesised by the exporter.
table_blocks.133: NULL (game type id 123). Unclaimed, and it bounds the rock block.
table_blocks.134-140: ROCK1..ROCK7 = ids 124-130, CONFIRMED by the same registration chain. Desert only.
table_blocks.55-91: civilian buildings V01..V37 (type_id 45-81) - CONFIRMED, and the calibration for the +10 offset
table_blocks.92-97: ROAD + the 5 wall types (SBAG/CYCL/BRIK/BARB/WOOD). NOT part of the unified enum: their records store 232-236, which is out of table range, consistent with walls being drawn as terrain overlays.

terrain_lookup.TC01_TC05: registered as real multi-cell terrain (occupy lists of 2,3,4,5,6 cells; strength 600) but with NO model index in ANY theater. The N64 build ships no tree-clump mesh, so there is nothing to draw and they stay fallbacks. This is a property of the ROM, not a gap in the dump.
terrain_lookup.bias: slot = id + 10, the same +10 that already applied to structures, vehicles and civilians. Independently re-confirmed here: the init loop at ROM 0x00571D8 walks 219 16-byte records from RAM 0x80099A38, which is exactly ten records past the 0x80099998 that work/table.json was enumerated from.
terrain_lookup.model_index_fields: three ints at sp+0x38 / sp+0x3C / sp+0x40 = the per-theater model index (desert / temperate / winter), -1 where the type does not exist in that theater. Where more than one is set they always hold the SAME index, so one mesh serves all theaters. ROCK1-7 and T04/T09/T18 are desert-only; T08 and SPLIT3 exist in all three. That matches Tiberian Dawn.
terrain_lookup.source: TerrainTypeClass registration chain, ROM 0x018CE30-0x018DE00, 32 calls to 0x801EAC0C, one per terrain type.
terrain_lookup.string_pool: ROM 0x169668 (CodeOverlay, RAM 0x801C7878): T01..T18, SPLIT2, SPLIT3, TC01..TC05, ROCK1..ROCK7 - 32 names, all 32 materialised by lui/addiu inside the chain, one block each.

APCDOOR.evidence: Code-derived. The APC's draw arm (resident ROM 0x0014BD4 / RAM 0x80013FD4) tests UnitType == 5 -- APC, read off the cartridge's own sixteen UnitTypeClass ctor calls at ROM 0x18B9EC..0x18C8D8 -- calls DoorClass::Door_Stage() at RAM 0x801D3C70 and issues a SECOND model command with model index 193 (ROM 0x0014BEC) before drawing the hull at the same position and yaw. 193 plus the +10 bias is model-table slot 203. Geometry corroborates: the child quad (+-107, 25.4, -259.2)-(+-107, 176.4, -271.2) is the APC hull's own rear face inset about 6.5 units and standing 13-15 proud, and its 16x16 CI8 texture at ROM 0x0F9D30 is used by no other slot in the ROM.

TRANRMP.evidence: Code-derived. The transport-helicopter draw arm (CodeOverlay ROM 0x0182358 / RAM 0x801E0568) gates on AircraftType == 0 -- TRAN, from the five AircraftTypeClass ctor calls at ROM 0x196164..0x1964AC -- calls Door_Stage() and issues model index 194 (ROM 0x0182360) before drawing the hull. 194 plus 10 is slot 204. The child quad fills the Chinook's tail under-slope.

P04.evidence: Code-derived, and the only entry here whose model the cartridge itself never names. WHAT IT IS: model-table slot 205 is scene-graph node RAM 0x801B8518, and the only 32-bit word in the whole ROM holding that node is that table entry at ROM 0x9B274. Its one display list 0x012DBC8 is 74 vertices and 60 triangles in four G_VTX batches. MEASURED EXTENT 826 x 329 x 690 mesh units, which is 0.81 x 0.32 x 0.67 WORLD CELLS at the renderer's cell of 1024 model units (game/cnc_eyes.cpp MODEL_SCALE = 1/1024; the independent check is a wall straight, authored x[-500,+501], i.e. 1001 units for one cell). For scale beside it: ORCA 588x325x1038 = 0.57 x 0.32 x 1.01 cells, HELI 429x297x1223, A10 1147x193x1054. An earlier version of this entry divided by 256 and reported 3.23 x 1.29 x 2.70 cells, which is wrong by 4x and would have made the flying Orca four cells long. Its y runs -70 to +259, so it sits IN the ground rather than on it. All 74 vertex colours are pure grey, measured: r = g = b on every one, 8 distinct levels between 49 and 255. Its single 16x16 CI8 texture at RAM 0x801262B0 (ROM 0x0CA5F0) is neutral to the texel as well: max |r-g| and max |g-b| across all 256 texels are both 0, mean 137, range 25..206. It decodes byte for byte identically under the GDI TLUT (ROM 0x98F30) and the neutral one (ROM 0x99130), so it is house independent. THAT TEXTURE IS SHARED, NOT EXCLUSIVE: walking every display list of the other 194 entries in this file, three of them bind RAM 0x801262B0 as well, namely HELI's hull (part 0, dl_0152FE0), HTNK's turret (part 1, dl_00D6A18) and five of SAM's seven parts (dl_00CDCA0, dl_00CD768, dl_00CD9A8, dl_00CDEA0, dl_00CDFF0). An earlier version of this entry claimed the texture was bound by exactly one other model and that the model was the Apache; that was measured FALSE and is corrected here. Reproduce with tools/bakery/render_dl.py --slot 205. WHAT THE SHAPE IS: a squat faceted airframe lying broken on the ground, nose dipped in, tail slab canted up, two wing panels torn outward and down. It is WIDER (826) than it is LONG (690), which no flying aircraft in the cartridge is. Recognised by eye as the crashed Orca of the console game; that recognition is a reading of pixels and is kept separate from the data on purpose, because the cartridge NEVER NAMES THIS MODEL. Its name catalogue is a word array of RAM pointers at ROM 0x1DE8FC indexed by model-table slot (self-calibrating: it lands GDI_UNIT_ORCAZ1 on slot 53 and ANY_TER_TR01Z1 on slot 113), and THE ENTRY FOR SLOT 205 IS ZERO, exactly as for 203 APCDOOR and 204 TRANRMP. An earlier version of this entry called that array "100 names at ROM 0x1B70F8" covering "slots 10..161 only", and that has to be taken apart rather than replaced. 0x1B70F8 is the address of nothing: the blob starts at ROM 0x1B7000 and 14 named slots (142, 143, 144, 151..161) point BELOW 0x1B70F8. "100 names" is not the count: over slots 10..161 the array points at 83 distinct strings, and over the whole array to slot 512, 115. "Slots 10..161" is true of the LOOKUP and false of the ARRAY: the model-name lookup at RAM 0x801D19B4 does stop at 152 entries, which is exactly 10..161, while the array itself keeps naming slots at 249..264, 277..279, 308..314, 319 and 332..334, the front end's BRF_* scene roots. Reading the lookup's bound as the array's extent is what put 205 "past the end" rather than at a zero entry inside it. A total depends on where the scan stops, and this file quotes two bounds because two independent scans reported them: over slots 0..319 the array names 179 slots holding 110 distinct strings, the last (BRF_3D_ARROW, slot 319) beginning at ROM 0x1B7A1C; carried on to slot 512 it names 184 slots holding 115 distinct strings across ROM 0x1B7000..0x1B7A84, the last two (413, 414) being ENGLISH and FRANCAIS and almost certainly a neighbouring array rather than models. Both are reproducible: --max-slot 320 and --max-slot 512. Reproduce with tools/bakery/name_catalogue.py. A ROM-wide scan for CRASH, WRECK, HULK, DEBRIS, HUSK or DOWNED returns only particle-system and animation names. The code P04 here is therefore the PC TEMPLATE's own name and not a cartridge name. WHAT DRAWS IT (ROM-derived): the cartridge keeps one cell-decoration draw table at RAM 0x8020FF58, 39 records of {mode, descriptor}, indexed by bits 15..20 of the cell object's word at +8. Entry 38 (descriptor RAM 0x8020FF40) is {195, -1}, and 195 + 10 is slot 205, the same +10 bias the walls and terrain use. The mode-2 path at RAM 0x801F57B4 reads that descriptor and the arm at RAM 0x801F5840 tests the base type against 195 and passes 1 instead of 0 in the sixth argument of the draw-queue call at RAM 0x801F5450 (record +0x0C). WHAT SELECTS IT (ROM-derived): not the type data. The 30 OverlayTypeClass registrations (ctor RAM 0x801F2F20, ROM 0x1950A8..0x195A18) and the 15 SmudgeTypeClass registrations (ctor RAM 0x801E8CE0, ROM 0x18ADEC..0x18B0A0) pass their draw index as the third constructor argument and between them claim every index except 0, 35 and 38; SCRATE claims 34 (the steel crate cube) and WCRATE 36 (the olive wooden one), which is what makes that argument's meaning certain rather than assumed. Entry 38 is reached from the TERRAIN. At theater load (RAM 0x801E5190) the game reads <THEATER>.TL4 and <THEATER>.TL8, two bytes per N64 tile slot holding the PC (template, icon) pair that slot was made from, scans both for the pair (70, 0) at RAM 0x801E5250 and RAM 0x801E52A4, and remembers that slot id through the setter at RAM 0x801F475C (ids below 1024 go to the TL4 list, the rest to the TL8 list minus 1024). The draw loop at RAM 0x801FB044 compares each cell object's tile id (bits 21..31 of the same word) against that remembered id and, on a match, forces draw index 38 with data 0 (the lui 0x13 at RAM 0x801FB06C is 38 << 15), draws, and restores the word. Yaw is 0 and the piece offset comes from entry 0 of the 16-entry connectivity table at RAM 0x802100D0, which is offset 0, so the model draws unrotated on its cell centre. WHICH TEMPLATE (EA GPL source, re-verified in this tree): TEMPLATE_PATCH4 is 70, counted from its own enum in tiberiandawn/defines.h, and tiberiandawn/cdata.cpp:1214 declares Patch4(TEMPLATE_PATCH4, THEATERF_TEMPERATE | THEATERF_DESERT, "P04", TXT_PATCH, LAND_ROCK, 1, 1, LAND_CLEAR, NULL): a 1x1 rock patch in temperate and desert only, which is where the theaters field above comes from. The cartridge's own tables agree: (70, 0) is DESERT.TL4 slot 841 and TEMPERAT.TL4 slot 18 and is absent from WINTER.TL8 and SNOW.TL8. So on the PC this cell is a flat grey rock patch and on the N64 it is a 3D wrecked airframe. WHICH MAPS (measured over the baked terrain data in this tree): 33 of the 96 terrain JSONs carry template 70 icon 0, 86 cells in all, 25 maps in desert and 8 in temperate. SCB33EA has 14, SCG62EA and SCM07EA 7 each, SCG10EA 2 at cells (18,32) and (38,44). HOW THE RENDERER FINDS THEM (measured against the shipped brain, not inferred): CNC_Get_Game_State(GAME_STATE_STATIC_MAP) fills CNCStaticCellStruct per cell with TemplateTypeName built as <IniName>_i<icon>.tga (tiberiandawn/dllinterface.cpp:2985), which is "P04_i0.tga" for exactly these cells, and CellClass::Get_Template_Info (tiberiandawn/cell.cpp:855) always returns true, so that array is dense and row-major over the exported rect. A probe that dlopens the shipped TiberianDawn.dylib and starts SCG10EA reads 849 non-clear cells and exactly 2 P04_i0.tga cells, matching the terrain JSON. BAKING: the baker walks every entry in this file regardless of the theaters field, so this mesh lands in EVERY pack; the theaters value records the PC template's own theater mask and gates nothing.
